assumptions.assumption: the picture buffer and the stream generator are part of the test wrapper, not of the block under test
assumptions.reason: the shell cannot present a stream; any design must provide the register map above

behaviour: AXI4-Stream video slave (tdata[7:0], tvalid, tready, tuser = start of picture, tlast = end of line), 80 x 60; the wrapper drives one pixel per clock and holds a pixel until tready.

Harris corner response with non-maximum suppression, as the course exercise: Sobel gradients scaled down by 4 (arithmetic shift), structure tensor summed over 3 x 3, k = 1/16, R = det - (trace*trace >> 4), signed 48-bit; threshold 50 000 000 (signed compare); the pixel is a corner if R is strictly greater than NW, N, NE, W and greater-or-equal than E, SW, S, SE; replicated borders (edge pixels extend the picture).
The corner pixels of the rectangles that are visible inside the picture, exactly (the bench accepts a detection within one pixel of each true corner, and no extra detections).
A rectangle only about 45 grey levels brighter than its surroundings gives a response below the threshold: no corners.

tests.text:
"""Acceptance tests of c13_nexys_harris_vga against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from model import COUNT, CORNER, DATA, DESIGN_ID, GO, PTR, SEL, STATUS, bench_pictures, check_corners, corners, pack_words


async def run_picture(b: Board, dut, name: str, img) -> None:
    exp = corners(img)
    await b.write(PTR, 0)
    for w in pack_words(img):
        await b.write(DATA, w)
    await b.write(GO, 1)
    await b.cycles(4800)
    for _ in range(600):
        if not (await b.read(STATUS)) & 1:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"{name}: still busy long after the picture")
    st = await b.read(STATUS)
    assert st & 2, f"{name}: no list available after the picture (STATUS 0x{st:X})"
    n = await b.read(COUNT)
    got = []
    for i in range(min(n, 64)):
        await b.write(SEL, i)
        v = await b.read(CORNER)
        got.append((v & 0x7F, (v >> 8) & 0x7F))
    why = check_corners(got, exp)
    assert not why, f"{name}: " + "; ".join(why) + f" (reported {got}, true {[tuple(c) for c in exp]})"
    assert n == len(got), f"{name}: the count is {n} but {len(got)} corners were readable"
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == n, f"{name}: LEDs show {led}, the count is {n}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    assert await b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    for off in (PTR, STATUS, COUNT, SEL, CORNER):
        await b.expect(off, 0, f"reset value of {off}")
    await b.write(PTR, 0x4AF)
    await b.expect(PTR, 0x4AF, "PTR is a plain register")
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == 0, f"LED {led:04X}: no corners yet"
    for off in (0x07, 0x41, 0x7F):
        await b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_course_picture_then_mixed_picture(dut):
    """The two bright rectangles of the course picture: eight corners, one detection each; then a different picture with strong, weak and edge-touching rectangles (the weak one has none)."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    for name, img in bench_pictures():
        await run_picture(b, dut, name, img)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_reset_forgets_the_list(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    await run_picture(b, dut, "before reset", bench_pictures()[0][1])
    await b.reset()
    for off in (STATUS, COUNT, SEL, CORNER):
        await b.expect(off, 0, f"register {off} after reset")
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == 0, f"LED {led:04X} after reset"

registers.bits: [10:0] word index of the parked picture (0..1199) that the next DATA write fills
registers.name: PTR

registers.bits: [31:0] four pixels of the parked picture at PTR (pixel 0 of the word in [7:0], row by row); PTR then increments; reads 0
registers.name: DATA

registers.bits: any write streams the parked picture (4800 pixels, row by row, tuser on pixel 0, tlast on the last pixel of each 80-pixel line) into the block, one per clock, and clears the list flag; reads 0
registers.name: GO

registers.bits: [0] BUSY: from GO until the list is final; [1] REPORT: a list is available (set when BUSY falls, cleared by GO and reset)
registers.name: STATUS

registers.bits: [15:0] number of corners found in the last picture (0 until a list exists); the LEDs show the same number
registers.name: COUNT

registers.bits: [5:0] place in the corner list that CORNER shows (0..63)
registers.name: SEL

registers.bits: [6:0] x and [14:8] y of corner SEL (the first 64 corners in raster order), valid a few clocks after SEL is written; 0 beyond COUNT
registers.name: CORNER

interface.reset: CPU_RESETN, active low: idle, no list, count 0, LEDs 0

mutants.name: gradient_scale
mutants.why: the horizontal gradient is scaled down by 2 instead of 4, so weak rectangles produce corners

mutants.name: threshold_too_high
mutants.why: the corner threshold is ten times too high, so medium-contrast corners are missed

mutants.name: threshold_too_low
mutants.why: the corner threshold is far too low, so faint rectangles produce corners

mutants.name: nms_west_dropped
mutants.why: the west neighbour is not part of the non-maximum suppression

mutants.name: nms_east_dropped
mutants.why: the east neighbour is not part of the non-maximum suppression

mutants.name: nms_south_dropped
mutants.why: the south neighbour is not part of the non-maximum suppression

mutants.name: nms_off
mutants.why: no non-maximum suppression: a cluster of detections at every corner

mutants.name: border_wraps
mutants.why: pixels left of or above the picture are taken from the opposite edge instead of replicated

mutants.name: count_double
mutants.why: the count of corners is twice the number found

mutants.name: x_and_y_swapped
mutants.why: the list holds y where x belongs

the LEDs (the count) equal the number of corners reported

spec_md:
# Corner finder behind the test shell

I want a block for the Nexys A7-100T's FPGA that finds the corners of the bright rectangles in a small picture, and I want to exercise it entirely from the test shell.

- The picture is 80 pixels wide and 60 high, 8-bit grey, and arrives as a stream of pixels, one per clock when available, row by row, with a start-of-picture mark and an end-of-line mark. It shows a few bright
  rectangles on a dark background; a different picture can follow.
- Find the corners of the rectangles. A corner is reported once, at the corner pixel: not along the edges, and not as a cluster of neighbouring pixels. Rectangles that are only faintly brighter than the background
  have no corners worth reporting. A rectangle that touches the edge of the picture has only the corners that are inside the picture; the edge of the picture itself is not a corner.
- When the picture has been processed, tell me how many corners were found and where each one is (x and y in whole pixels, x counted from 0 at the left and y from 0 at the top), as a list I can read.
- The 16 LEDs show, in binary, how many corners were found in the picture.
- The red CPU reset button returns the block to idle and forgets the list.

The shell is slow, so the stream is driven for me: I park a whole picture over the shell (four pixels per write, row by row, the first pixel of a word in its lowest byte) and give a "go" command, and the block
then presents the pixels to the stream, one per clock. A status flag says busy from "go" until the list is final, and another says that a list is available. I read the number of corners, and then the corners one
at a time (I select a place in the list and read it). The shell runs at 115200 baud on the USB-UART. The design ID is "HARR".

Test hooks: top module `c13_nexys_harris_vga_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, and the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters as top-level parameters. There are no other time
constants.

trace.stimulus: The 80 by 60 picture with 2 bright rectangles on a dark background. The model computes the corner response everywhere and keeps the local peaks above the threshold.

what: A corner detector for a small grey-scale picture. It measures how brightness changes around each pixel in two directions, combines the measurements into a corner score, and keeps only scores that are high and are the largest nearby, so that each corner is reported once. The result is a list of corner positions, and the LEDs show how many were found.
where: Harris corner detection is a classic first step in feature tracking, image stitching, camera calibration and visual odometry. FPGAs run it on streaming video where a processor would be too slow.
